messages.author: 2e06c863f78200c0
messages.subject: Shiny server and ui
parts:
I have been making an r package that uses shiny interfaces as demos and they work great. The one problem I have is that there seems to be some hoops I have to jump through if I want more that one demo. For instance I cannot have multiple server.R and ui.R files in the demo directory. I can have multiple files called from demo that can run multiple interactive shiny demos, but they have to jump through hoops to point to the correct server and ui files. It also gets rather difficult to track multiple files with the same name. I investigated the source code and it seems the runApp() function I use calls the startApp() function. This has two lines that set the server.R and ui.R files.
uiR <- file.path.ci(getwd(), 'ui.R') 
serverR <- file.path.ci(getwd(), 'server.R') 
Is there a reason that these are hard-coded to these names. Would it be more robust if you could pass runApp() two arguments which would also be passed to startApp(). They could be defaulted by runApp(ui = 'ui.R', server = 'server.R') if you give it the directory, but you can then have more flexibility by being able to call runApp(appDir = 'dir') directory or runApp(ui = MY'ui.R', server = 'MYserver.R'). Or it would even open the door to using an actual function as an argument. Since server.R consists of a shinyServer() which wraps a function you could pass the function as an argument, you could have logic before hand that could modify the function based on the circumstances. This could give different interfaces based on the data or other parameters involved.

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server and ui
parts:
runApp also takes a list as an argument

runApp(list(
  ui = ... ,
  server = ... 
))

So you can write your own custom wrapper if you want to achieve something like runApp(appDir = 'dir')
